blocks.md:
Here is a short poem written for this lesson.

*Rain on the zinc roof, tap, tap, tap, tap, tap. Rain on the green leaves, splash, splash, splash, splash, splash. The street is a river, the children all cheer. Rain, rain, stay and play! We are so glad you are here.*

blocks.caption: The first two lines of the poem and its sound words.
blocks.alt: The lines Rain on the zinc roof, tap tap tap tap tap and Rain on the green leaves, splash splash splash splash splash, with the sound words tap and splash named below.

blocks.title: Parts of a poem
blocks.md: A poem is written in **lines**. A group of lines is a **stanza**. Words that **rhyme** end with the same sound: *cheer - here*. **Rhythm** is the beat of the lines. **Sound words** (onomatopoeia) sound like what they mean: *tap, splash, buzz, bang*. A poet may repeat words to make a pattern.

blocks.title: Reading a poem aloud
blocks.md: Read slowly. Pause at commas and full stops. Make your voice **soft** for quiet lines and **loud** for happy lines. Say the **sound words** with feeling. Ask: *What picture do I see? How does the poet feel?*

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that words rhyme because they begin alike: rhyme comes at the **end** (cheer - here).
- Reading a poem like a list, without pauses.
- Saying only what the poem is about, without saying how it feels.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Find a pair of rhyming words in: 'The children all cheer. We are so glad you are here.'
steps: Look at the last word of each line.
Cheer and here end with the same sound.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name two sound words from the poem.
steps: Read the poem and look for words that sound like their meaning.

blocks.title: Polite words
blocks.md: Use polite words every day. **Greetings**: *Good morning, Good afternoon, Good evening, Hello.* **Asking**: *Excuse me, please. May I come in? Could you help me?* **Thanking**: *Thank you (very much). You are welcome.* **Saying sorry**: *I am sorry. That is all right.* Look at the person and speak in a clear voice.

items.text: How are you? I am fine, thank you.
Excuse me, please. Thank you very much.
I am sorry. That is all right.

blocks.caption: Polite expressions for everyday talking.
blocks.alt: Four boxes with polite phrases: greetings, asking how someone is, excuse me and thank you, saying sorry.

blocks.title: Sounds
blocks.md: Some words differ only by a **short** or **long** vowel: **ship / sheep**, **bit / beat**, **full / fool**, **pull / pool**. Listen carefully and say them slowly. Also practise the **th** sounds in *thank* and *this*, and say the **ends** of words clearly: *hand, bed, cold*.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Speaking too fast or too softly, so that nobody can hear.
- Forgetting *please* and *thank you*.
- Dropping the end of a word: *han* instead of *hand*.
- Mixing words that sound alike (ship/sheep).

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What do you say when you enter the headmaster's office?
steps: First knock, then say a polite sentence.
Excuse me, sir. May I come in, please?
blocks.answer: Excuse me, sir. May I come in, please?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Which word has the long vowel: 'ship' or 'sheep'?
steps: In 'sheep' the vowel is long: sheeeep.

exercises.prompt: Write four lines about rain or sun. Use at least two rhyming words and one sound word.
exercises.model:
The sun is hot, the sky is blue,
The birds all sing, 'tweet, tweet, too!'
We play outside, the day is bright,
And we go home when comes the night.
exercises.rubric: Marks (4): four lines (1); at least one pair of rhyming words (1); a sound word (1); the poem makes sense and has a feeling (1).

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Write a short conversation (4 lines) between a pupil and the teacher when the pupil arrives late.
exercises.model:
Pupil: Good morning, Madam. I am sorry I am late.
Teacher: Good morning, Ako. Why are you late?
Pupil: The bus was late, Madam.
Teacher: All right. Please sit down quietly. Thank you.
exercises.rubric: Marks (4): a greeting (1); an apology (1); a reason (1); polite words (please / thank you) and correct punctuation (1).
